title: Wisdom of Solomon, Chapter 18
language: Greek (Codex Sinaiticus) / English (King James Version Apocrypha)
source: Codex Sinaiticus folio + transcription (codexsinaiticus.org) + King James Version Apocrypha (1611; 1769 text)
description: Wisdom of Solomon chapter 18. Manuscript page scan(s) from Codex Sinaiticus hosted by the Codex Sinaiticus Project, with the Project's verbatim transcription of the Greek and the English of King James Version Apocrypha (1611; 1769 text).
introduction:
This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: The actual folio(s) of Codex Sinaiticus containing this chapter, from the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). Each section links to the specific folio holding its verses.
  2. Original text: The Codex Sinaiticus Project's verbatim transcription of the folio shown (uncial letters, lunate sigma, nomina sacra preserved).
  3. English translation: King James Version Apocrypha (1611; 1769 text), public domain, retrieved verbatim from ebible.org eng-kjv USFM (KJV with Apocrypha).

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>τοιϲ δε οϲιοιϲ ϲου . μεγιϲτον ην φωϲ ων φωνην μεν ακουοντεϲ · μορφην δε ουχʼ ορωντεϲ οτι μεν ουν κακεινοι επεπονθιϲαν · εμακαριζον <sup>2</sup>οτι δ ου βλαϲτουϲιν · προηδικημενοι · ευχαριϲτουϲιν και του διενεχθηναι · χαριν οδοντων <sup>3</sup>ανθ ων πυριφλεγη ϲτυλον ολιγον μεν · αγνωϲτου οδοιποριαϲ ηλιον δε αβλαβη φιλοτιμιαϲ παρεϲχε <sup>4</sup>αξιοι μεν γαρ εκεινοι ϲτερηθηναι φωτοϲ · και φυλακιϲθηναι ϲκοτουϲ οι κατακλιϲτουϲ φυλαϲϲοντεϲ . τουϲ υϊουϲ ϲου δι ων εμελλεν το αφθαρτον νομου φωτοϲ · τω αιωνι διδοϲθαι · <sup>5</sup>βουλευϲαμενουϲ αυτουϲ · τα των οϲιων αποκτινειν νηπια και ενοϲ εκτεθεντοϲ τεκνου · και ϲωθεντοϲ ειϲ ελεγχον το αυτων · αφειλω πληθοϲ τεκνων τουϲ δε εχθρουϲ του λαου ομοθυμαδον · απωλεϲαϲ εν ϋδατι ϲφοδρω <sup>6</sup>εκινη η νυξ · προεγνωϲθη πατραϲιν ημων ϊνα αϲφαλωϲ ειδοτεϲ · οιϲ επιϲτευϲαν ορκοιϲ · επιθυμηϲωϲιν <sup>7</sup>προϲεδεχθη υπο λαου ϲου ϲωτηρια μεν δικαιων · εχθρων δε απωλια · <sup>8</sup>ωϲ γαρ ετιμωρηϲω τουϲ υπεναντιουϲ τουτω ημαϲ προϲκαλεϲαμενοϲ . εδοξαϲαϲ
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>Nevertheless thy saints had a very great light, whose voice they hearing, and not seeing their shape, because they also had not suffered the same things, they counted them happy. <sup>2</sup>But for that they did not hurt them now, of whom they had been wronged before, they thanked them, and besought them pardon for that they had been enemies. <sup>3</sup>Instead whereof thou gavest them a burning pillar of fire, both to be a guide of the unknown journey, and an harmless sun to entertain them honourably. <sup>4</sup>For they were worthy to be deprived of light and imprisoned in darkness, who had kept thy sons shut up, by whom the uncorrupt light of the law was to be given unto the world. <sup>5</sup>And when they had determined to slay the babes of the saints, one child being cast forth, and saved, to reprove them, thou tookest away the multitude of their children, and destroyedst them altogether in a mighty water. <sup>6</sup>Of that night were our fathers certified afore, that assuredly knowing unto what oaths they had given credence, they might afterwards be of good cheer. <sup>7</sup>So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies. <sup>8</sup>For wherewith thou didst punish our adversaries, by the same thou didst glorify us, whom thou hadst called.

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>κρυφη γαρ εθυϲιαζον οϲιοι παιδεϲ αγαθων και τον τηϲ οϲιοτητοϲ νομον · εν ομονοια διεθεντο · των αυτων ομοιωϲ και αγαθων και κινδυνων · μεταλημψεϲθαι τουϲ αγιουϲ πρων · ηδη προαναμελποντων αινουϲ · <sup>10</sup>αντηχει δ αϲυμφωνοϲ εχθρων η βοη και οικτρα διεφερετο φωνη · θρηνουμενων παιδων <sup>11</sup>ομοια δε δικη · δουλοϲ αμα δεϲποτη κολαϲθειϲ και δημοτηϲ βαϲιλεια ταυτα παϲχων <sup>12</sup>ομοθυμοαδον παντεϲ · εν ενι ονοματι θανατου νεκρουϲ ειχον · αναριθμητουϲ ˙ ουδε γαρ προϲ το θαψαι · οι ζωντεϲ ηϲαν ϊκανοι · επι προϲ μιαν ροπην · εντιμοτερα γενεϲειϲ αυτων διεφθαρτο · <sup>13</sup>παντα γαρ απιϲτουντεϲ δια ταϲ φαρμακιαϲ επι τω των πρωτοτοκων ολεθρω · ωμολογηϲαν θυ ϋϊον λαον ειναι · <sup>14</sup>ηϲυχου γαρ ϲειγηϲ περιεχουϲηϲ τα παντα και νυκτοϲ · εν ϊδιω ταχει μεϲαζουϲηϲ · <sup>15</sup>ο παντοδυναμοϲ ϲου λογοϲ απ ουρανων · εκ θρονων βαϲιλιων · αποτομοϲ πολεμιϲτηϲ · ειϲ μεϲον τηϲ ολεθριαϲ ηλατο γηϲ ξιφοϲ οξυ · την ανϋποκριτν επιταγην ϲου φερων · <sup>16</sup>και ϲταϲ · επληρωϲεν τα παντα θανατου και ουρανου μεν ηπτετο . βεβηκει δε γηϲ
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>For the righteous children of good men did sacrifice secretly, and with one consent made a holy law, that the saints should be like partakers of the same good and evil, the fathers now singing out the songs of praise. <sup>10</sup>But on the other side there sounded an ill according cry of the enemies, and a lamentable noise was carried abroad for children that were bewailed. <sup>11</sup>The master and the servant were punished after one manner; and like as the king, so suffered the common person. <sup>12</sup>So they all together had innumerable dead with one kind of death; neither were the living sufficient to bury them: for in one moment the noblest offspring of them was destroyed. <sup>13</sup>For whereas they would not believe any thing by reason of the enchantments; upon the destruction of the firstborn, they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God. <sup>14</sup>For while all things were in quiet silence, and that night was in the midst of her swift course, <sup>15</sup>Thine Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction, <sup>16</sup>And brought thine unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death; and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth.

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>τοτε παραχρημα φανταϲιαι μεν ονιρων δεινων · εξεταραξαν αυτουϲ φοβοι δε · επεϲτηϲαν αδοκητοι · <sup>18</sup>και αλλοϲ αλλαχη ριφιϲ ημιθνητοϲ δι ην εθνηϲκον αιτιαν · ενεφανιζεν <sup>19</sup>οι γαρ ονιροι θορυβηϲαντεϲ αυτουϲ . προεμηνυϲαν ϊνα μη αγνοουντεϲ δι ο κακωϲ παϲχουϲιν · απολωνται <sup>20</sup>ηψατο δε και δικαιων τοτε . πιρα θανατου και θραυϲειϲ εν ερημω . εγενετο πληθουϲ αλλ ουκ επι πολυ εμινεν η οργη ϲου <sup>21</sup>ϲπευϲαϲ γαρ ανηρ αμεμπτοϲ . προεμαχηϲεν το τηϲ ϊδιαϲ λιτουργιαϲ οπλον · προϲευχην και θυμιαματοϲ · εξιλαϲμον κομιϲαϲ αντεϲτη θυμω . και περαϲ επεθηκεν τη ϲυμφορα δεικνυϲ · οτι ϲοϲ εϲτιν θεραπων · <sup>22</sup>ενικηϲεν δε τον οχλον · ουκ ϊϲχυει του ϲωματοϲ · ουχ οπλων ενεργεια αλλα λογω · τον κολαζοντα ϋπεταξεν ορκουϲ πατερων και διαθηκαϲ · ϋπομνηϲαϲ <sup>23</sup>ϲωρηδον γαρ ηδη πεπτωκοτων επ αλληλων νεκρων μεταξυ ϲταϲ · ανεκοψεν την οργην και διεϲχιϲεν · την προϲ τουϲ ζωνταϲ οδον <sup>24</sup>επι γαρ ποδηρουϲ ενδυματοϲ ην · ολοϲ ο κοϲμοϲ και πρων δοξαι · επι τετραϲτιχου λιθου γλυφη και μεγαλωϲυνη ϲου · επι διαδηματοϲ κεφαληϲ αυτου
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>Then suddenly visions of horrible dreams troubled them sore, and terrors came upon them unlooked for. <sup>18</sup>And one thrown here, and another there, half dead, shewed the cause of his death. <sup>19</sup>For the dreams that troubled them did foreshew this, lest they should perish, and not know why they were afflicted. <sup>20</sup>Yea, the tasting of death touched the righteous also, and there was a destruction of the multitude in the wilderness: but the wrath endured not long. <sup>21</sup>For then the blameless man made haste, and stood forth to defend them; and bringing the shield of his proper ministry, even prayer, and the propitiation of incense, set himself against the wrath, and so brought the calamity to an end, declaring that he was thy servant. <sup>22</sup>So he overcame the destroyer, not with strength of body, nor force of arms, but with a word subdued him that punished, alleging the oaths and covenants made with the fathers. <sup>23</sup>For when the dead were now fallen down by heaps one upon another, standing between, he stayed the wrath, and parted the way to the living. <sup>24</sup>For in the long garment was the whole world, and in the four rows of the stones was the glory of the fathers graven, and thy Majesty upon the diadem of his head.

translation.original_text: <sup>25</sup>τουτοιϲ ειξεν ο ολοθρευων · ταυτα δε εφοβηθηϲαν ην γαρ μονη η πιρα τηϲ οργηϲ ϲου · ϊκανη
translation.text: <sup>25</sup>Unto these the destroyer gave place, and was afraid of them: for it was enough that they only tasted of the wrath.
